build_notes: TOOLCHAIN: Python 3.8+.

LANGUAGE CONCERNS: (1) Use 'asyncio' + 'websockets' for the async model. (2) Use 'uuid.uuid4()' for UUID generation. (3) Use 'enum.Enum' for the state representation. (4) Outbound store should be a 'dict' keyed by 'msg_id'. (5) Inbound store should be a 'set' of 'msg_id' strings for deduplication. (6) Use type hints on all public methods. (7) Use 'json.dumps' and 'json.loads' for JSON wire serialization.

ENTRY POINT: client.py serves as both the MessagingClient library and the runnable entry point. There is no separate runner file. At the bottom of client.py, add an `if __name__ == '__main__':` block that imports sys, sets up WARNING-level logging, and runs an async `_main()` function via `asyncio.run(_main())`.

USER INTERFACE LOOP: Inside `_main()`, prompt the user with `input('Chat as: ')` for username. Server URL is fixed to ws://localhost:8765 — do not prompt for it. Define an async `on_message(from_user, body)` callback that prints `<- [from_user] body` and reprints the prompt. Initialize and connect MessagingClient. Then run a readline loop prompting with `<username>> `.
To prevent blocking the asyncio event loop on Windows, input is read asynchronously using the event loop's executor: `await loop.run_in_executor(None, input, f'{username}> ')`.

INPUT COMMANDS: The loop parses input: 'exit' or 'quit' terminates the client (calling `await client.disconnect()`); `<recipient> <message>` sends a message using `await client.send_message(recipient, message)`. Any other input displays an error message.

AUTO-RECONNECT: MessagingClient must include automatic reconnection with exponential backoff. Add fields `_auto_reconnect: bool` (set True in initialize(), False in disconnect()) and `_reconnect_delay: float` (start 1.0, double each attempt, cap at 30.0, reset to 1.0 on success). In the `_recv_loop` finally block, if `_auto_reconnect` is True, schedule `asyncio.ensure_future(self._do_reconnect())`. `_do_reconnect()` loops: log warning, sleep delay, call `connect()`, reset delay on success. On each failed attempt set state back to DISCONNECTED and continue the loop.

post_generate.unix: mkdir -p gradle/wrapper && curl -sL -o gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar https://github.com/gradle/gradle/raw/v8.7.0/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar && chmod +x gradlew
post_generate.note: gradle-wrapper.jar is a binary and cannot be generated as text. This command downloads it from the official Gradle GitHub repo. Run from within output_dir.

build_notes: TOOLCHAIN: Kotlin 1.9.24, Gradle 8.7 wrapper (distributionUrl=https://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-8.7-bin.zip), compileOptions JavaVersion.VERSION_17, kotlinOptions jvmTarget '17'.

LANGUAGE CONCERNS: (1) Use 'kotlinx.coroutines' + OkHttp/Ktor WebSockets for the async model. (2) Use 'java.util.UUID.randomUUID()' for UUID generation. (3) Use 'enum class' for the state representation. (4) Outbound store should be a 'ConcurrentHashMap' keyed by 'msg_id'. (5) Inbound store should be 'Collections.newSetFromMap(ConcurrentHashMap())' for deduplication. (6) Use data classes for message models. (7) Use 'org.json' for JSON wire serialization.

IMPORTS: Main.kt must import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking. MessagingClient.kt must import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking, kotlinx.coroutines.sync.Mutex, kotlinx.coroutines.sync.withLock, and all other used coroutine and Ktor symbols explicitly.
PLUGINS: kotlin("jvm") version "1.9.24"; application.

settings.gradle.kts: pluginManagement { repositories { mavenCentral(); gradlePluginPortal() } }; dependencyResolutionManagement { repositoriesMode.set(RepositoriesMode.FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS); repositories { mavenCentral() } }; rootProject.name = 'minmessage-cli'.
gradle.properties: org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx2g -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 | kotlin.code.style=official.

gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties: distributionBase=GRADLE_USER_HOME | distributionPath=wrapper/dists | distributionUrl=https\://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-8.7-bin.zip | networkTimeout=10000 | validateDistributionUrl=true | zipStoreBase=GRADLE_USER_HOME | zipStorePath=wrapper/dists.
gradlew and gradlew.bat: standard Gradle 8.7 wrapper shell scripts. Generate the canonical Gradle wrapper script content for Unix (gradlew) and Windows (gradlew.bat).

WEBSOCKET: use Ktor client with OkHttp engine: val client = HttpClient(OkHttp) { install(WebSockets) }. Connect with client.webSocket(wsUrl) { ... }. Session type: DefaultClientWebSocketSession. Read frames: for (frame in incoming) { if (frame is Frame.Text) handleFrame(frame.readText()) }. All session.send(...) calls MUST be wrapped inside sendMutex.withLock { ... } to serialize concurrent writes.
LOCAL STORAGE: In-memory outbound queue using ConcurrentHashMap<String, OutboundEntry>() and inbound history using Collections.newSetFromMap(ConcurrentHashMap()). No database persistence required.

MAIN CLI LOOP: Main.kt runs a CLI application. On start, it prompts the user with 'Chat as: ' on standard input. It reads the username, then instantiates and starts MessagingClient (defaulting the WebSocket URL to ws://localhost:8765). It runs a blocking readline loop on the main thread, supporting commands: `/quit` (break loop), `/status` (print connection status), and `@recipient message text` (send a message via coroutine `runBlocking { client.sendMessage(to, body) }`).

STDIN FORWARDING: build.gradle.kts MUST include a tasks.named<JavaExec>("run") block that sets standardInput = System.`in`. Without this, Gradle does not forward stdin to the JVM process and the readline loop exits immediately. Place this block before the dependencies block: tasks.named<JavaExec>("run") { standardInput = System.`in` }.

AUTO-RECONNECT: MessagingClient must include automatic reconnection with exponential backoff. Add fields `autoReconnect: Boolean` (set true in initialize(), false in disconnect()), `reconnectDelayMs: Long` (start 1000, double each attempt, cap at 30000, reset to 1000 on success), and `reconnectJob: Job?`. In the session coroutine's finally block, set state to DISCONNECTED if CONNECTED or CONNECTING, null the session, then if `autoReconnect && reconnectJob?.isActive != true` launch `doReconnect()` in scope. `doReconnect()` loops with delay, calls `connect()`, resets delay on success. In `disconnect()`, set `autoReconnect = false` and cancel `reconnectJob` before closing the session.
